explanations.answer: Cities to live in with pasturelands
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. The LORD tells Moses to have the Israelites give "cities for the Levites to live in and pasturelands around the cities" (Numbers 35:2). A home with grazing land out back. Most adults would sign that lease before reading it.

explanations.answer: A strip of land by the Great Sea
explanations.explanation: Beachfront would be something, I'll give you that. But the LORD tells Moses to have the Israelites give cities and pasturelands, not a strip of land (Numbers 35:2). Those cities come out of the inheritance the Israelites will possess.

Israel is camped across from Jericho (Numbers 35:1), so I see why that one tempts you. But the LORD says to give "cities for the Levites to live in and pasturelands around the cities" (Numbers 35:2). The Levites' land is cities with grazing land around them.

Refuge it is, baker. The LORD says six of the Levites' cities are "to be appointed as cities of refuge, to which a manslayer may flee" (Numbers 35:6). A refuge is a shelter, a spot where someone can find protection. So the same cities the Levites live in carry this job too.

Worship is a fair guess, since these are Levite cities. But the LORD names a different job: "cities of refuge, to which a manslayer may flee" (Numbers 35:6). A refuge is a shelter. That's the word the verse uses.
Gathering sounds friendly, I know. But the word in the verse is a different one: "cities of refuge, to which a manslayer may flee" (Numbers 35:6). A refuge is a shelter for someone fleeing.

Not quite, friend. The LORD says the cities are to be given "in proportion to the inheritance of each tribe: more from a larger tribe and less from a smaller one" (Numbers 35:8). So a big tribe gives more cities and a small tribe gives fewer. It's like chipping in for cookie boxes, where the one with the big batch hands over more.

Right, baker, it's false. The LORD says the cities are given "in proportion to the inheritance of each tribe: more from a larger tribe and less from a smaller one" (Numbers 35:8). Big tribe, more cities. Small tribe, fewer. Same pie, different slices.

explanations.answer: Someone who kills a person by accident
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. The cities are for "a person who kills someone unintentionally" (Numbers 35:11). It's someone who never meant any harm. I think that's a heavy thing to carry, and the LORD provides a place for him to flee.

explanations.answer: Someone who kills a person on purpose
explanations.explanation: That's the other side, friend. The cities are for "a person who kills someone unintentionally" (Numbers 35:11). Later the LORD says that if someone strikes "in hostility" and the person dies, "he is a murderer" (Numbers 35:21). So the refuge isn't for the one who kills on purpose.

explanations.answer: Someone who kills an enemy in battle
explanations.explanation: The LORD says nothing about battle here. He says the cities are for "a person who kills someone unintentionally" (Numbers 35:11). That's the one the refuge is set up for.
That's right, baker. The cities are there "so that the manslayer will not die until he stands trial before the assembly" (Numbers 35:12). The verse names the assembly, so that's who he stands before.
No king shows up in this verse, friend. The LORD says the manslayer "stands trial before the assembly" (Numbers 35:12). The assembly is who the verse names.
Prophets aren't named here, friend. The LORD says the manslayer will not die "until he stands trial before the assembly" (Numbers 35:12). So the assembly is the answer.

Close, friend, but they're split up. The LORD says, "Select three cities across the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan as cities of refuge" (Numbers 35:14). So three of them are across the Jordan. Three and three is an even split, the kind of math I can actually handle.

Right, baker. The LORD says, "Select three cities across the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan as cities of refuge" (Numbers 35:14). Three on each side. An even split, the kind of math I can actually handle.

That's right, baker. "These six cities will serve as a refuge for the Israelites and for the foreigner or stranger among them" (Numbers 35:15). Anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there. I like that the refuge isn't for one group only.

The text says otherwise, friend. "These six cities will serve as a refuge for the Israelites and for the foreigner or stranger among them" (Numbers 35:15). So the foreigner is included. Anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.

explanations.answer: He must be put to death
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Whether it's an iron object, a stone of deadly size or a deadly object of wood, the LORD says "he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death" (Numbers 35:16-18). Each of the three verses says it the same way. I think this is one of the heavy parts.

explanations.answer: He must pay the family back
explanations.explanation: Paying back isn't what the LORD says here. For these cases, "the murderer must surely be put to death" (Numbers 35:16). Later He adds, "You are not to accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die" (Numbers 35:31). So no payment takes the place of it.

explanations.answer: He must be sent out of the land
explanations.explanation: Being sent out of the land isn't in these verses, friend. The LORD says, "he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death" (Numbers 35:16-18). That's the same line for the iron object, the stone and the wood.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, "The avenger of blood is to put the murderer to death; when he finds him, he is to kill him" (Numbers 35:19). That's said of the murderer. I think it's a heavy verse to read.

The LORD says it plainly, friend: "The avenger of blood is to put the murderer to death; when he finds him, he is to kill him" (Numbers 35:19). So it's true. This one is said of the murderer. It's a heavy verse.

Yes, baker. The LORD says that if "in hostility he strikes him with his hand and he dies, the one who struck him must surely be put to death; he is a murderer" (Numbers 35:21). The verse names hostility, and it names a plain hand. I think that's a serious one.

The text says otherwise, friend. The LORD says that if "in hostility he strikes him with his hand and he dies, the one who struck him must surely be put to death; he is a murderer" (Numbers 35:21). So a hand alone, struck in hostility, still counts. It's a heavy verse.

explanations.answer: Protect him from the avenger of blood
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. "The assembly is to protect the manslayer from the hand of the avenger of blood" (Numbers 35:25). Then the assembly returns him to the city of refuge he fled to. I think that's a lot of care for someone who did not intend to harm anyone (Numbers 35:23).

explanations.answer: Hand him over to the avenger of blood
explanations.explanation: It's the opposite, friend. The LORD says, "The assembly is to protect the manslayer from the hand of the avenger of blood" (Numbers 35:25). So the assembly stands between the manslayer and the avenger. Then it returns him to the city of refuge he fled to.

explanations.answer: Make him pay the family a fine
explanations.explanation: A fine isn't mentioned here. The LORD says, "The assembly is to protect the manslayer from the hand of the avenger of blood" (Numbers 35:25). After that, the assembly returns him to the city of refuge he fled to.

Yes, baker. The manslayer lives in his city of refuge "until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil" (Numbers 35:25). The LORD says it again: "Only after the death of the high priest may he return to the land he owns" (Numbers 35:28). So he stays in the city until then.
A word from the high priest isn't what the verse names, friend. The manslayer lives in the city of refuge "until the death of the high priest" (Numbers 35:25). The word that fits the blank is death.

A blessing would be lovely, but it's not what the verse says. The manslayer lives in the city of refuge "until the death of the high priest" (Numbers 35:25). The LORD repeats it in verse 28: only after the death of the high priest may he return to the land he owns.

The text says otherwise, friend. If the avenger finds him outside his city and kills him, "then the avenger will not be guilty of bloodshed" (Numbers 35:27). The LORD gives the reason: "because the manslayer must remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest" (Numbers 35:28). I think this is a sobering one.

Right, baker, it's false. If the avenger finds the manslayer outside his city of refuge and kills him, "then the avenger will not be guilty of bloodshed" (Numbers 35:27). The LORD gives the reason: "because the manslayer must remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest" (Numbers 35:28). I think this is a sobering one.

Yes, baker. A murderer is put to death "on the testimony of the witnesses," and the LORD adds, "But no one is to be put to death based on the testimony of a lone witness" (Numbers 35:30). One voice alone isn't enough. It takes more than one.
A lone witness is exactly what the LORD rules out. He says, "no one is to be put to death based on the testimony of a lone witness" (Numbers 35:30). So one isn't enough, and it takes more than one.

Witnesses are needed, friend. The LORD says the murderer is put to death "on the testimony of the witnesses" (Numbers 35:30). And he adds that no one is put to death on the word of a lone witness. So it takes more than one.

That's right, baker. The LORD says, "You are not to accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die; he must surely be put to death" (Numbers 35:31). The verse is plain and gives no way around it. I think it's a heavy one.

explanations.answer: Accept it if the family agrees
explanations.explanation: The verse doesn't hand the family that choice, friend. The LORD says, "You are not to accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die; he must surely be put to death" (Numbers 35:31). So no ransom is accepted.

explanations.answer: Accept it once a priest approves
explanations.explanation: A priest's approval isn't in this verse, friend. The LORD says, "You are not to accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die; he must surely be put to death" (Numbers 35:31). So no ransom is accepted.

Verse 32 says otherwise, friend. The LORD says, "Nor should you accept a ransom for the person who flees to a city of refuge and allow him to return and live on his own land before the death of the high priest" (Numbers 35:32). So no ransom buys him an early trip home. He waits for the death of the high priest.

Right, baker, it's false. The LORD says, "Nor should you accept a ransom for the person who flees to a city of refuge…" (Numbers 35:32). The verse goes on that he is not to return and live on his own land before the death of the high priest. So he waits for that.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, "Do not pollute the land where you live, for bloodshed pollutes the land, and no atonement can be made for the land on which the blood is shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it" (Numbers 35:33). It's a heavy verse. The word that fits the blank is blood.

An offering isn't the word the verse gives, friend. The LORD says "no atonement can be made for the land on which the blood is shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it" (Numbers 35:33). It's a heavy verse. The word that fits is blood.

Prayer isn't what this verse names, friend. The LORD says "no atonement can be made for the land on which the blood is shed, except by the blood of the one who shed it" (Numbers 35:33). It's a heavy verse. The word that fits is blood.

That's right, baker. The LORD says, "Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell. For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites" (Numbers 35:34). It's the land where they live and where He dwells. That's the reason He gives.

explanations.answer: Their crops will not grow there
explanations.explanation: Crops don't come up in this verse, friend. The reason the LORD gives is this: "For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites" (Numbers 35:34). He also says the land is where they live and where He dwells.

explanations.answer: Other nations will hear of it
explanations.explanation: Other nations aren't mentioned here, friend. The reason the LORD gives is this: "For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites" (Numbers 35:34). He also says the land is where they live and where He dwells.
